required_fixes: RF1 — Tenant-setup parity gap (endpoint overrides and reviewed tenant import). Location: feature-baseline.md:16 lists v1 'endpoint overrides, verification/import/reset' and source-evidence.md:42-44 cites src/cli_tenants.rs review-before-import; parity-matrix.md:9 closes the row with only 'context/capability separation, explicit verification and reset'; C02 milestones/acceptance cover neither; test-catalogue.md:25-27 (T05) denies 'custom endpoint changes that would forward a credential' and 'implicit environment/tenant file loading' without saying how the legitimate v1 endpoint-override and explicit reviewed tenant-import workflows are kept. Impact: a working v1 workflow could be silently dropped, or T05 could be implemented in a way that forbids it. Nothing tells an implementer whether nonsecret v1 tenant profiles (labels/endpoints) are C02 explicit imports or C23 'settings'. Acceptance: name an owning chunk (C02 and/or C23) and add milestones and acceptance for (a) explicit operator-reviewed endpoint overrides bound to a credential destination allowlist, with T05 wrong-origin denial still enforced, and (b) explicit reviewed tenant-profile import (nonsecret fields only; fresh credential entry per D015), or record an owner decision to retire them. Update the parity-matrix row and C23 category list to match.

RF2 — D016 offline behavior is only planned for Academy. Location: decisions.md:185-193 (D016 covers local drafts, saved work, history and downloaded Academy content, with no silent replay of configuration changes, scans, grading or other remote actions); C07 and T12 are Academy-only; no chunk or test ID asserts offline launch and use of non-Academy saved work (cases C12, FP/FN reports C11, API Client documents C14, Harness protected history C20, pending configuration drafts/reviews C09/C10/C17), or no replay on reconnect for those features. C24 milestones do not mention offline. Impact: an accepted cross-feature decision has no owning acceptance criterion, so stable could pass without D016 being shown outside Academy. Acceptance: add a cross-feature offline test (a new T-ID or an expansion of T03/T12) and bind it to the owning chunks plus a cumulative C24 milestone. It must assert: offline launch; read/edit of each local-work category; pending reviews/scans/inference/tool calls are not resubmitted after reconnect; explicit retry is offered; uncertain outcomes are kept.

RF3 — Performance budgets cover only first-slice workloads, and the rules for later budgets are undefined. Location: C03.md:23, test-catalogue.md:92-95 (T20), IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md:169 and C24.md:11,22 set budgets in C03 only. C24 then 're-runs' large-list, streaming and active-Harness workloads that do not exist at C03, so they have no previously committed budget. No rule says who sets or approves budget values, or how a budget may be loosened. Impact: later workloads can get budgets set after measurement (fitted to pass), which undercuts D020's 'budgets before broad rollout' intent and makes the C24/C26 regression gates vacuous for those workloads. Acceptance: require each chunk that introduces a named workload (e.g. C11/C13 large collections, C18 streaming, C19–C21 Harness) to commit its numeric budget and method before its measurement acceptance. Require recorded rationale plus owner or reviewer acknowledgement in the receipt for any budget change. State that C24/C26 compare against those pre-committed values.

RF4 — There is no defined, owner-approved mandatory live-check list, so C25 live scope is open-ended. Location: C25.md:27 ('feature-specific IDs ... as applicable'), C26.md:22,27 ('controlled final-artifact live smoke' with undefined content), release-contract.md:16-34 and parity-matrix.md:36-48. Only C22.md:47 names a specific mandatory live item (MCP). Impact: stable readiness depends on 'designated live acceptance', but nothing fixes which parity rows require live evidence, so live scope could shrink at C25 time to whatever access exists. That conflicts with D022 and the plan's own 'missing access blocks' rule. Acceptance: G01/C01 per-workflow parity expansion must mark each row's live requirement (required / not required, with reason / blocked-by-access), and the owner must approve that list before C25. Define the C26 final-artifact smoke set explicitly. Any reduction requires a recorded owner scope decision rather than being reported as 'not applicable'.

RF5 — No gate covers v2's outbound distribution license and the right to redistribute shared Academy source. Location: D001 (public distribution), source-evidence.md:24-28 (framework license has commercial/fork conditions) and 176-178 (Academy has no license and is `private: true`), dependencies.md:27-31 (notices only, 'rather than inventing a license'), C26 milestone 1 (inventory notices only). Nothing assigns the owner decision on the license and terms under which the public v2 DMG ships, or written confirmation that Academy shared presentation (and any adapted framework code) may be publicly redistributed inside it. Impact: a signed public release could be blocked or non-compliant late in C26, and the shared-package extraction in C01 might be designed before redistribution rights are known. Acceptance: add an explicit G01 output (and C26 release precondition) recording the owner-selected v2 license/distribution terms, the Academy redistribution permission, and the framework-derived code disposition, with a release-blocking check that the shipped notices inventory matches it.

RF6 — The API Client raw-request admission policy is delegated to G01 but missing from G01's exit criteria. Location: C15.md:21 says 'define conservative raw-request admission in G01'. architecture-handoff.md:31-32 lists it only as an exploration priority; the 'Required selected-design outputs' (architecture-handoff.md:51-68) and prompts/architecture.md do not list it ('Exact native IPC/command admission' is a different concern). Impact: G01 could pass without the policy that keeps generic HTTP from bypassing Rust review authority with managed AIRS credentials (a core D014 authority surface). C15 would then be unexecutable or improvised. Acceptance: add to the handoff's required outputs and the architecture prompt a specified admission policy. It must cover classification of known Prisma mutation endpoints, the default for unclassified requests carrying managed credentials, destination/redirect binding, and the negative tests C15 must run.
optional_suggestions: Strict numeric ordering (IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md:61-64, chunks/README.md:3-4) means pending SDK Phase 5/6 (dependencies.md:48-52) blocks C13 and everything after it, including C19–C23, which partly do not depend on those SDK families. This is consistent with D018 and not a defect. Consider stating explicitly that a long dependency stall is escalated to the owner as a reorder/scope decision (per decision-tree.md:47-49) instead of waiting indefinitely.

C01 builds the controller that validates C01's own receipt. Say how the C01 receipt is bootstrapped and checked: for example, by having the reviewer read the controller's negative-test evidence before the controller first gates itself.

Identify in dependencies.md whether v2's independent identity needs new or changed hosted OAuth client registrations (Academy device client, Harness company-SSO loopback redirect, MCP clients), and who owns those changes. C04 and C20 forbid production registration changes, so this is an external dependency that should be visible before C25.

Classify the v1 Runtime PI/directionality local-preview options (feature-baseline.md:39) in a specific chunk (likely C08/C09) so they are explicitly carried as previews rather than discovered during the parity expansion.

Several UI chunks (e.g. C04 device-flow UI, C08 onboarding, C16) do not list T09 even though IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md:170 says every UI chunk includes keyboard/focus checks. Add T09 to their acceptance lists for consistency.

Say whether preview DMGs (release-contract.md:8-10) must be signed/notarized, and which chunk produces the 'approved versioned precursor' build that C26's rollback test depends on (release-contract.md:83-86).

C16.md:11 says 'accepted complete SDK Phase6 read/configuration subset'. Align the wording with dependencies.md:51-52 ('need not claim every unrelated SDK method') to avoid being read as requiring all of Phase 6.
